name: bank-sanctions-backlog
title: Bank sanctions-hit backlog: a burst of listed names
description: A burst of payments names parties that closely resemble entries on a fictional sanctions list. Screening holds them, a review queue builds up in the operations console, and a manager's approval is needed before any of them can move.

steps.title: An ordinary morning
steps.narration: Customers of a retail bank are sending money abroad as usual. Every payment is screened against the sanctions list before anything else happens, and almost all of them pass straight through.

steps.title: A burst of near-matches arrives
steps.narration: Now a burst of payments to companies whose names are spelled slightly differently from listed entities. Each one on its own is easy to miss. Together they start to form a queue.

steps.title: Senders with listed-looking names
steps.narration: A second wave: senders in the UK whose names resemble listed individuals. Screening holds these too, before any money moves.

steps.title: The review queue builds up
steps.narration: Open the operations console: held payments appear as sanctions cases, each showing the list entry, how close the match is and the deadline for a decision. This is the backlog an analyst team has to work through.

steps.title: Four eyes on every release
steps.narration: An analyst can only recommend a release or a rejection. A manager must approve it, and every step goes into the append-only audit trail. Nothing is posted to the ledger until that decision is made.

expected.text: At least 10 payments name a party resembling a listed entry.
At least 8 crafted payments flow on US-IN.
Sanctions cases for the listed-name payments appear in the operations console review queue.
Held payments show no ledger posting until a manager approves a release.
